copy_cases.name: valid_discovery_t1_cold_storage
copy_cases.old_failure: none — positive control inside the 60–95 word band
copy_cases.subject: Power checks at Brampton cold storage
copy_cases.body:
Hi Dana,

Your site list shows six refrigerated warehouses across Ontario and Alberta. When one loses grid power overnight, does maintenance confirm the utility event themselves before deciding generator runtime, or is that already in the alarm chain? OutageHub matches Canadian utility outage reports to a location and time through an API. I'm trying to learn whether that removes a real lookup or duplicates what you have.

Even a short reply either way helps.

Andrew Gordienko

copy_cases.name: one_hundred_fifty_word_t1
copy_cases.subject: Power checks at Brampton cold storage
copy_cases.body:
Hi Dana,

Your site list shows six refrigerated warehouses across Ontario and Alberta, which is a substantial operating footprint by any measure, and it made me think carefully about what happens inside your organization on a difficult winter night. When one of those warehouses loses grid power overnight, somebody on your team presumably has to figure out what actually happened, whether it is a utility event or an equipment failure, how long it might last, whether the generators have enough runtime, whether inventory is at risk, and who needs to be told about all of it. That is a lot of coordination under pressure. OutageHub matches Canadian utility outage reports to a location and a time through an API, which could conceivably help with several of those steps in various ways. Would you be open to a twenty minute conversation about how your team handles all of this today?

Andrew Gordienko
